answer: Sybil defense by per-identity cost: each new agent identity must stake a deposit tied to reputation. Newcomers start at zero trust, so the economy caps their weight. Attesting is risky, so honest agents form a trellis of endorsements, not a flat vote; fresh accounts cannot self-attest, since each endorsement shifts liability to the endorser. Faking ten thousand identities costs ten thousand deposits, and one caught twin forfeits the cluster. Attack cost climbs while the flood yields nothing, a river of wasted fees. Only a costly opal of verified history converts stake to influence.
